clue.text: Commercial designs go alongside flower

explanation.definitionFit: Pop art is the 1950s-60s movement built from advertising and packaging imagery, so its works are commercial designs in style.

clue.text: Male chauvinists on television initially in colour

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word television

explanation.surface: Sexist men appearing on TV, broadcast in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a substance that gives colour, so the word stands for colouring matter.

clue.text: Ring around last quarter of yard — this under a foot?

explanation.definitionFit: A pedal, on a bike or piano, is a lever worked by pressing down with the sole of a shoe.

clue.text: Alumnus tucked in to Indian bread on top of chicken jerky

explanation.walkthrough: 'jerky' looks like dried meat beside the chicken, but it is the definition: moving in jerks.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic movement is stiff and mechanical, and jerky motion is likewise abrupt and unsmooth.

clue.text: Sharapova's weapon, loud noise

definitions.meaning: Maria Sharapova is a tennis champion whose weapon is her strung bat

explanation.surface: A tennis star's weapon makes a loud noise, as her famous grunting did.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tennis player's strung bat and a noisy din.

clue.text: Forest close to desert, hot

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the word desert

explanation.surface: A forest lying near a desert, sweltering.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate or burning, and hot can mean eager and fervent in the same way.

clue.text: Privileged youth supporting the board — that's a footballer's skill

explanation.surface: A rich youngster backing the board, with a nod to a football trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the board' looks like a company's directors, but means keep, as in board and lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Keepy-uppy is the trick of juggling a ball in the air with feet, knees and head without it touching the ground.

clue.text: Work to hold in food, primarily, as food wrapper

parts.note: toil is hard work

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter of the word food

explanation.definitionFit: Tinfoil is thin metal sheet used for covering and wrapping things to eat.

clue.text: Swimmer getting on in sport

parts.note: the skate is a flat fish, a swimmer
boarding is getting on a bus, ship or plane

explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person in the pool; here it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a wheeled deck is a recreational and competitive sport.

clue.text: At first disgusting, time to withdraw Shakespearean oath

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: At first takes the opening letter of disgusting

explanation.surface: Something revolting at first, and time to retreat: an old exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an archaic mild oath, a softened 'by God', of the kind heard in old plays.

clue.text: With starters for Bed and Breakfast, sneaked off to get tinned food

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged
starters for asks for the opening letter of each of Bed, and, Breakfast

explanation.surface: Someone slips away from a B&B to buy a can of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the shuffle of B, A, B with SNEAKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Haricots in tomato sauce are the classic canned food, a staple of the British breakfast.

clue.text: Cut fruit about right, then time to make wine

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened fruit goes round the letter for right
cut says the fruit word loses its last letter

parts.note: a melon is a fruit

explanation.surface: Chop the fruit, turn right, then it's time to make wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' removes N from MELON, leaving MELO, which goes 'about' R.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlot is a red grape variety and the red wine made from it.

clue.text: Recall curious novel's introduction, a source of information for poet

indicators.note: recall, read as re-call or call back, says the following string is read backwards

parts.note: nosy means curious, prying

indicators.note: introduction takes the opening letter of the word novel's

parts.note: the net, the internet, is a source of information

explanation.surface: Remember a nosy novel's opening and the internet's help, for a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' looks like 'remember', but read as call back it turns the whole string around, not just the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was Victorian Britain's Poet Laureate, writer of The Charge of the Light Brigade.

clue.text: Flavoured item in farm animals, 8 say?

parts.note: livestock, stock, are farm animals
8 is two cubed, an example of a cube number

explanation.surface: Something tasty found among cattle, maybe eight of them.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' looks like a count of animals; it is a cube number.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock cube is a pressed block of dried seasoning used to flavour soups and gravy.

clue.text: Refuse to move slowly, as winger

parts.note: chaff is husks and waste, refuse
to inch is to move little by little

explanation.surface: A footballer on the wing declines to speed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb, to decline; it is the noun, rubbish. 'winger' suggests a footballer but means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaffinch is a common European finch, and a bird is a creature with wings.

clue.text: Round pearl regularly seen as gem that's white, perhaps?

parts.note: a round thing is O-shaped

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of pearl, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A round pearl, often seen as a white gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone found in white, black and fire varieties, so white is one example.

clue.text: Cloth from the East includes Eastern clothing

indicators.note: includes says the reversed cloth word holds the letter inside
in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: a rag is a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Fabric imported from the Orient, including Eastern dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is informal for clothes, as in 'get your gear on'.

clue.text: Relative almost passing round a European city

indicators.note: passing round says the shortened relative goes round the letter a
almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a grandad is a relative

explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts GRANDAD to GRANDA, which wraps A.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada is a city in Andalusia, Spain, home of the Alhambra.

clue.text: Touring the country, capital drained of hot African water

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the shortened capital surrounds the country
drained of says the capital loses the letter for hot

parts.note: Lhasa is the capital of Tibet

Kenya is an African country

explanation.surface: On a tour of the country, the capital runs dry of heat beside African waters.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is Tibet's, and 'drained of hot' removes its H; what remains is split around the country by 'Touring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Nyasa is the old name of Lake Malawi, a great East African lake.

clue.text: Extraordinary area is covering Uzbek capital — that's a lot of land!

extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged
capital means the first, upper-case letter of Uzbek

explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinary' gives ERASIA, and 'covering' wraps that round the U, which sits second.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is the combined landmass of Europe and Asia, the largest on Earth.

clue.text: Pink Floyd's last member standing in Scotland

parts.note: salmon is a shade of pink

indicators.note: last asks for the end letter of Floyd's

explanation.surface: The final remaining member of the band Pink Floyd, in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink Floyd' reads as the band; split it: pink is a colour, Floyd gives D. 'standing' means as an election candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Alex Salmond, former First Minister, stood for and sat as a member of the Scottish Parliament.

clue.text: A third of debris in tip is heavy

explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' suggests a rubbish dump, but is the verb, to tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden literally means made of lead, so heavy, dull and weighty.

clue.text: US president, a two-dimensional pussy

definitions.meaning: James A. ... was the 20th President of the United States
a flat cartoon cat, the lasagne-loving comic-strip feline

explanation.surface: An American leader who is a flat cat.

clue.text: Puzzle that's full of holes?

clue.text: Inventor of the vacuum flask, part inside warmer?

clue.text: Byzantine daintiness in Paris commune

clue.text: Question, then answer — stop!

parts.note: who is a question word

explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the call to a horse to halt, and more generally a cry to stop or slow down.

explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.

clue.text: Not all there, free capital

to rid is to free
